items.title: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner 

Bitcoin Core developers have disclosed and patched a medium-severity bug that let an attacker temporarily freeze a node’s processing of blocks and transactions, a flaw first flagged by an AI scanner built by Block’s Spiral.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-117348, is fixed in Bitcoin Core versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1. The 30.5 and 31.3 releases shipped Friday alongside the public advisory, while 32.1 has carried the fix since Oct. 27.

Affected versions run from 29.0 through 29.5, 30.0 through 30.4 and 31.0 through 31.2. The 29.x series has reached end of life and will not get a fix, so operators on that branch need to move to a newer release.

How the Core bug worked 

Bitcoin Core keeps “orphan” transactions, whose parent transactions it has not yet seen, and asks peers that announce them for the missing pieces. Since version 29.0, the software builds a list of an orphan’s parents and checks each one against its mempool and filters before deciding what to request.

A single inv message can carry up to 50,000 entries, and the software did not skip duplicates. An attacker could send a node an orphan with thousands of missing parents, then send messages repeating that transaction’s ID 50,000 times.

“Each such message stalls the node for over a dozen seconds, during which it processes no messages from other peers, including blocks,” the advisory said. Sending more messages could stretch the disruption out.

The fix makes the node process each transaction announced in an inv message…
items.t: Bitcoin Core Patches Node-Stall Bug Found by Block’s AI Scanner

items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Bitcoin Price Surges Above $64,000 as Nvidia Reinstates CEO 

The bitcoin price surged to above $64,000 on Monday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive and sent stocks sharply higher. Bitcoin is up about $8,500 from its weekend low of roughly $55,100, which came at about 1:17 a.m. ET on Saturday.

Nvidia’s board voted unanimously to bring Huang back as president, CEO and director, effective immediately, the company said Monday morning. The board said it spoke with Huang and received input from “senior levels of the United States government,” concluding that his return “poses no national security risk.”

Nvidia board restores Huang after 12 days 

Huang resigned on Nov. 11 after reports of an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence officials believe is a Chinese spy. CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO. The board has said an investigation into the reported foreign intelligence effort will continue, and Huang said he supports it.

Nvidia chair Harvey Jones said the board believes Huang “is the right person to lead” the company. Huang called it an honor to return and said he “can’t wait to get back to work.” The company also formed a national security and export control committee and is searching for a chief compliance officer.

The stock had lost nearly half its value during a seven-week losing streak, even after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly results on Nov. 17. Investors worried about life without Huang, and bitcoin traded in step with the rout in technology shares.

items.title: UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

UK FCA Bars Crypto Exchanges From Market Making on Their Own Venues 

The U.K. will bar crypto exchange operators from trading against their own capital on the venues they run, while a new Treasury order clears independent market makers to trade on those platforms without a separate dealing permission.

The Financial Conduct Authority’s final rules say a firm “must not execute any orders against its proprietary capital” on a qualifying trading platform it operates. The FCA’s guidance spells out the effect: a firm “cannot act as a market maker” on its own platform. The restriction takes effect Oct. 25, 2027.

The FCA rule itself is not new. The regulator published it on June 30 in policy statement PS26/11, part of a five-document package that completed its crypto rulebook. What changed last week was the Treasury’s side of the framework.

What the FCA rule covers 

The FCA’s rulebook defines a market maker as a person who holds themselves out on a platform on a continuous basis as willing to buy and sell qualifying cryptoassets against their own capital at prices they set. That is the activity operators will be barred from on their own venues.

There is one carve-out. An operator with the appropriate permission may still engage in matched principal trading to execute client orders on its platform, as long as it follows the platform’s non-discretionary rules. The FCA warned that this model does not rule out settlement risk, so firms should take steps to minimize it.

The bar applies only to the operator’s own platform. Under the same rules, an operator with…

items.title: Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

Strategy (MSTR) Adds 457 Bitcoin for $29.6 million 

Strategy (MSTR) bought 457 bitcoin last week for $29.6 million at an average of about $64,898 per coin, an 8-K filing shows, lifting its total to 851,305 BTC as the bitcoin price trades about under the company’s average cost.

The purchase ran from Nov. 16 to Nov. 22. Strategy said it paid $64.23 billion for its stack, an average of $75,446 per coin including fees and expenses. That is $6 below the $75,452 average it reported a week earlier, so the new coins barely moved the cost basis.

The buy is also smaller than the 485 bitcoin Strategy added the week before . Strategy shares were trading near $83.50 in premarket on Monday, up about 7% from Friday’s close near $78.

How Strategy paid for the coins 

Strategy funded the purchase entirely with common stock. It sold 1,925,676 MSTR shares under its at-the-market program for net proceeds of $176.7 million, and no preferred stock was sold during the week.

Only $29.6 million of that cash went into bitcoin. The rest went to buy back Strategy’s own STRC preferred stock, which is the pattern the company has followed for several weeks.

Strategy repurchased 2,183,747 STRC shares for $211.8 million. It paid $147.0 million of that with MSTR proceeds and $64.8 million from its USD Cash balance. The preferred buyback was roughly seven times the bitcoin spend.

The board also lifted the size of its digital credit securities repurchase program from $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion. After the increase, $1.12 billion remains available. About $17.9 billion of MSTR stock…

items.title: American Bitcoin (ABTC) Lands $150 Million Bitcoin-Backed Credit Line From FalconX
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

American Bitcoin (ABTC) Lands $150 Million Bitcoin-Backed Credit Line From FalconX 

American Bitcoin Corp. (ABTC) has secured a $150 million revolving credit facility from FalconX that is backed by its bitcoin, the miner said Monday, giving it a way to raise cash without selling coins from its reserve.

The facility was signed by an American Bitcoin subsidiary and is secured by certain of the company’s bitcoin holdings. American Bitcoin said the money can go toward strategic growth opportunities and general corporate purposes. “This $150 million facility provides American Bitcoin with non-dilutive capital to support our continued operations and growth initiatives,” CEO Mike Ho said in the release.

Terms of the FalconX facility 

The FalconX line is committed up to $150 million, and each draw is subject to bitcoin collateral requirements and other customary conditions. Because it is revolving, the company can draw, repay and redraw funds during the term.

Borrowings carry a 5.95% loan fee, plus a commitment fee on any undrawn amount. The initial term is two years, with an optional three-year extension at FalconX’s discretion, subject to customary conditions. The company did not name the size of the commitment fee.

The facility has an initial collateral ratio of 143%. At that level, drawing the full $150 million would require about $214.5 million in pledged bitcoin, or roughly 3,500 BTC with bitcoin trading near $61,300 early Monday.

American Bitcoin did not say whether it has drawn on the line yet. Its release lists the risks, including the possible…

items.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
items.summary:
Bitcoin Magazine 

SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme 

The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading.

The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme.

Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets.

They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange.
